goal: Review the manifest telemetry schema/contract changes in the uncommitted local diff for shape stability, naming, severity semantics, and backward compatibility.
background: Review target: uncommitted working-tree changes (git diff HEAD).
Changed files (tracked, modified), paths relative to bakeoff/ context root:
Primary surface for this lens: internal/manifest/manifest.go and the consumer side referenced by internal/commands/doctorcmd/doctor_test.go.

Companion lenses run separately: correctness (code defects) and docs-tests (doc accuracy + test coverage). This lens focuses ONLY on telemetry schema, contract, and downstream coupling — not pure code defects or doc prose.
Known context: untracked work-order files reference 'manifest-telemetry-highest-severity', indicating the change likely adds a highest-severity field to manifest telemetry.

facet.focus: Evaluate the manifest telemetry schema changes for stability, clarity, and safe evolution.
include: JSON/serialized field names, casing, and pluralization consistency with existing manifest fields
field types and nullability: are zero values, empty strings, or missing fields semantically distinguishable for downstream consumers
severity vocabulary: enum coverage, ordering semantics, tie-breaking rules, default for empty input
backward compatibility: do existing manifest consumers (doctor, history, inspect, downstream tooling) continue to parse correctly when the new field is absent or unknown
schema versioning: should schema_version or a manifest version bump accompany the new field
hidden coupling: any consumer code or fixtures that depend on the manifest shape and were not updated
documentation of the field contract (in code comments, struct tags, or doc files) versus implicit behavior
exclude: general correctness bugs outside the schema contract (covered by correctness lens)
documentation prose quality and test coverage gaps (covered by docs-tests lens)
style preferences without project convention evidence
large refactors unrelated to the changed schema surface
